facts.fact_text: On 23 July 2007, Hyde Park applied to the Municipal Council of Chișinău for authorisation to stage a protest on 30 August 2007.
The planned protest of 30 August 2007 was to be staged in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office.
The planned protest of 30 August 2007 was against alleged acts of harassment of Hyde Park by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office.
On 20 August 2007, the Municipal Council of Chișinău authorised the protest planned for 30 August 2007.
The Municipal Council of Chișinău authorised the protest to be staged in front of the building of the Ministry of Internal Affairs between 7.30 a.m. and 8.15 a.m. on 30 August 2007.
The Municipal Council of Chișinău authorised the protest to be staged in front of the Prosecutor General's Office between 8.15 a.m. and 9 a.m. on 30 August 2007.
The authorisation required the protest to be held at a distance of at least fifty metres from the buildings of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office.
On 30 August 2007, at 7.30 a.m., the applicants started their protest in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
Immediately after the applicants started their protest on 30 August 2007, a police officer approached them and ordered them to stop the protest.

The police officer ordered the applicants to stop the protest because the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 had been challenged by the Prosecutor General's Office in court on 29 August 2007.
The police officer argued that according to the Law on the Prosecutor's Office, the prosecutor's appeal against an administrative act suspended the latter's action until after a court examined it.
The applicants refused to comply with the police officer's order to stop the protest on 30 August 2007.
The applicants argued that the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 was valid and that their protest was peaceful.
The applicants relied on the provisions of the Constitution of Moldova and on the Convention in support of their argument that the protest was lawful.
Shortly after the applicants refused to comply, a police van arrived at the scene of the protest on 30 August 2007.
Mr Ghenadie Brega was arrested on 30 August 2007 and taken to a police station where he was questioned.
Mr Oleg Brega was arrested on 30 August 2007 and taken to a police station where he was questioned.
Mr Hristea-Stan was arrested on 30 August 2007 and taken to a police station where he was questioned.
Mr Juraveli was arrested on 30 August 2007 and taken to a police station where he was questioned.
At approximately 9.30 a.m. on 30 August 2007, Mr Ghenadie Brega, Mr Oleg Brega, Mr Hristea-Stan and Mr Juraveli were released without explanation.
The applicants could not continue their protest on 30 August 2007 because the time indicated in the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation had lapsed.
On 30 August 2007, a criminal complaint was lodged against the police officers who carried out the arrests of Mr Ghenadie Brega, Mr Oleg Brega, Mr Hristea-Stan and Mr Juraveli.
The criminal complaint against the police officers who carried out the arrests on 30 August 2007 was dismissed by the head of the police station of the Centru District on 19 September 2007.

The head of the police station of the Centru District dismissed the criminal complaint on the ground that the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 contained numerous flaws, including a failure to indicate the exact place of the protest.

The head of the police station of the Centru District dismissed the criminal complaint on the ground that the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 failed to indicate the number of participants.
The Prosecutor General's Office's appeal against the Municipal Council of Chișinău's authorisation of 20 August 2007 appears never to have been examined by the courts.

On 30 August 2007, Mr Juraveli, the vice-president of Hyde Park, applied to the Municipal Council of Chișinău for an authorisation to stage a protest in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office between 4 and 11 September 2007.
The planned protest between 4 and 11 September 2007 was against the allegedly abusive suppression of Hyde Park's peaceful protest of 30 August 2007.
In the application for authorisation for the protest between 4 and 11 September 2007, Mr Juraveli indicated that ten persons were to participate in the demonstration.
In the application for authorisation for the protest between 4 and 11 September 2007, Mr Juraveli gave his own name as one of those responsible for the conduct of the demonstration.
In the application for authorisation for the protest between 4 and 11 September 2007, Mr Juraveli gave the name of Mr Oleg Brega as one of those responsible for the conduct of the demonstration.
In the application for authorisation for the protest between 4 and 11 September 2007, Mr Juraveli gave the name of Mr Hristea-Stan as one of those responsible for the conduct of the demonstration.
The Municipal Council of Chișinău did not adopt a decision in respect of Mr Juraveli's application of 30 August 2007 before the first date of the planned demonstration, 4 September 2007.
At 9 a.m. on 4 September 2007, the applicants started their protest in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
At 9.25 a.m. on 4 September 2007, Mr Ghenadie Brega was arrested on the ground that the demonstration had not been authorised.
At 9.25 a.m. on 4 September 2007, Mr Oleg Brega was arrested on the ground that the demonstration had not been authorised.
At 9.25 a.m. on 4 September 2007, a Hyde Park member who is not an applicant in the present case was arrested on the ground that the demonstration had not been authorised.
Mr Ghenadie Brega, Mr Oleg Brega and the non-applicant Hyde Park member were taken to a police station on 4 September 2007 where they were body searched.
Mr Ghenadie Brega, Mr Oleg Brega and the non-applicant Hyde Park member were kept at the police station for approximately five hours on 4 September 2007.
According to the applicants, the police examined and made copies of the detained persons' documents, including personal letters, on 4 September 2007.
Two of the persons detained on 4 September 2007 were placed in cages and later in cells at the police station.
The persons detained on 4 September 2007 were later taken to the Centru District Court.
Since the hearing at the Centru District Court was adjourned, the persons detained on 4 September 2007 were released at 3 p.m. that day.
On 21 September 2007, the Centru District Court examined the charges against the applicants arising from the demonstration of 4 September 2007.

The applicants argued before the Centru District Court that since the Municipal Council of Chișinău had failed to examine their application for authorisation before the date of the demonstration, they had the right to hold the demonstration in accordance with section 12(5) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995.

The applicants submitted to the Centru District Court that they had been told by a representative of the local authorities that the Municipal Council of Chișinău did not have time to deal with their request and that they could hold their protest as planned.
The Centru District Court dismissed the applicants' submissions regarding the demonstration of 4 September 2007.

The Centru District Court found that the applicants had breached section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 by failing to submit the application within fifteen days in advance of the planned assembly.
According to the Centru District Court, the protest should have been held on 14 September 2007 at the earliest.
The Centru District Court found Mr Ghenadie Brega guilty of organising an unauthorised demonstration and fined him 800 Moldovan lei (approximately 48 euros).
The Centru District Court found Mr Oleg Brega guilty of organising an unauthorised demonstration and fined him 800 Moldovan lei (approximately 48 euros).
Another Hyde Park member who is not an applicant in the present case was fined 200 Moldovan lei by the Centru District Court in connection with the demonstration of 4 September 2007.
The applicants appealed against the Centru District Court's judgment regarding the demonstration of 4 September 2007.
The applicants' appeal was dismissed by the Chișinău Court of Appeal on the same grounds on 23 October 2007.
On 7 September 2007, the Municipal Council of Chișinău examined Mr Juraveli's application of 30 August 2007 for authorisation to stage a protest.

On 7 September 2007, the Municipal Council of Chișinău issued an authorisation to Mr Juraveli to organise and stage a protest in front of the buildings of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office between 8 and 11 September 2007.
In the morning of 10 September 2007, several members of Hyde Park started to protest in front of the buildings of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Prosecutor General's Office.

Several minutes after the Hyde Park members began protesting on 10 September 2007, the police arrived and arrested Mr Juraveli on the ground that the authorisation did not contain the names of all the persons involved in the protest.

Several minutes after the Hyde Park members began protesting on 10 September 2007, the police arrived and arrested Mr Oleg Brega on the ground that the authorisation did not contain the names of all the persons involved in the protest.

Several minutes after the Hyde Park members began protesting on 10 September 2007, the police arrived and arrested Mr Hristea-Stan on the ground that the authorisation did not contain the names of all the persons involved in the protest.

The Government maintained that Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan had been detained on 10 September 2007 for breach of the peace and for having shouted insults about the Minister for Internal Affairs.
At the police station on 10 September 2007, Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan were questioned and searched.
Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan were released after five hours of detention on 10 September 2007.
The applicants maintained that, while detained on 10 September 2007, they were not allowed to make any telephone calls or to contact a lawyer.
The police filed administrative proceedings against Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan following their arrest on 10 September 2007.

On 21 September 2007, the Centru District Court decided to discontinue the administrative proceedings filed against Mr Juraveli, Mr Oleg Brega and Mr Hristea-Stan in connection with the events of 10 September 2007.
On 5 September 2007, Mr Oleg Brega wrote to the Prosecutor General making a criminal complaint in respect of the actions of the police at the demonstration of 30 August 2007.
On 5 September 2007, Mr Oleg Brega wrote to the Prosecutor General making a criminal complaint in respect of the actions of the police at the demonstration of 4 September 2007.
A further letter to the Prosecutor General regarding the criminal complaint about police actions at the demonstrations of 30 August and 4 September 2007 was sent on 10 January 2008.
The applicants maintain that they did not receive an official response to either letter sent to the Prosecutor General on 5 September 2007 and 10 January 2008.

Section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that not later than fifteen days prior to the date of the assembly, the organiser shall submit a notification to the Municipal Council.

Section 11(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall indicate the name of the organiser and the aim of the assembly, the date, starting time and finishing time, the location and access and return routes, the manner in which the assembly is to take place, the approximate number of participants, the persons responsible for the sound conduct of the assembly, and the services the organiser asks the Municipal Council to provide.

Section 11(3) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that if the situation so requires, the Municipal Council may alter certain aspects of the prior notification with the agreement of the organiser of the assembly.

Section 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall be examined by the local government of the town or village at the latest five days before the date of the assembly.

Section 12(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that when the prior notification is considered at an ordinary or extraordinary meeting of the Municipal Council, the discussion shall deal with the form, timetable, location and other conditions for the conduct of the assembly and the decision taken shall take account of the specific situation.

Section 12(6) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local authorities can reject an application to hold an assembly only if, after having consulted the police, it has obtained convincing evidence that the provisions of sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act will be breached with serious consequences for society.

Section 14(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that a decision rejecting the application for holding an assembly shall be reasoned and presented in writing, and shall contain reasons for refusing to issue the authorisation.
Section 15(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the organiser of the assembly can challenge the refusal in the administrative courts.

Section 19 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that participants at the assembly are required to respect the Act and other laws referred to therein, to respect the instructions of the organiser of the assembly and decisions of the municipality or police, and to leave the assembly if asked by the organiser, the municipality or the police.

Article 166(1) of the Criminal Code of Moldova provides that illegal deprivation of liberty, if it is not a kidnapping, shall be punishable with community work of 120-240 hours or imprisonment of up to 2 years.

Article 166(2) of the Criminal Code of Moldova provides that illegal deprivation of liberty committed against two or more persons or by two or more persons shall be punishable with imprisonment of 3 to 8 years.

Article 184(1) of the Criminal Code of Moldova provides that violation of the right to freedom of assembly by way of illegal hindering of a demonstration, rally or action of protest or hindering of persons from taking part in them, when committed by an official, by two or more persons, or accompanied by acts of violence which are not dangerous to life or health, shall be punishable with a fine of four to eight thousand Moldovan lei or with community work of 180-240 hours, or with imprisonment of up to two years.

Article 174 § 1(2) of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provided that the organisation and holding of an assembly without prior notification to the Municipal Council or without authorisation from the Council, or in breach of the conditions concerning the conduct of meetings indicated in the authorisation, shall be punishable by a fine on the organisers (leaders) of the assembly in an amount equal to between 500 and 1,000 Moldovan lei.

Article 174 § 1(4) of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provided that active participation in an assembly referred to in paragraph 2 of Article 174 § 1 shall be punishable by a fine in an amount between 200 and 300 Moldovan lei.

Article 174 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provided that resisting a police officer in the exercise of his or her duties of ensuring public order and the fight against crime shall be punishable by a fine up to 300 Moldovan lei or detention of up to thirty days.

Article 174 § 6 of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provided that insulting police officers in the exercise of their duties shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200 Moldovan lei or imprisonment of up to fifteen days.
